newsitem.title: GERMANY: Details of Thyssen, Krupp steel merger.
newsitem.headline: Details of Thyssen, Krupp steel merger.

text.p: Statements made by industrial groups Thyssen AG and Krupp Hoesch and the state of North Rhine-Westphalia provided the following details on Wednesday about the planned merger of their steel businesses.
The new company will be operational on April 1 and Thyssen will have a majority stake of 60 percent, with Krupp holding the remaining 40 percent.

The new company's total workforce will fall to 18,000 by the year 2002, down from a combined workforce of 26,000 today. It will produce 15 million tonnes of crude steel per year and be Europe's largest maker of flat steel products.
Of the estimated 8,000 jobs that will be cut, nearly 4,000 will come from Krupp Hoesch Stahl operations, mainly at its Dortmund facilities, where its blast furnace operations will be shut down.
The other 4,000 job cuts are not directly related to the merger, but are the result of previously agreed cuts in areas where Krupp and Thyssen already co-operate.
The new company is considering investing up to one billion marks in the Dortmund works, broken down as follows:
-- 250 million marks for a new hot dip galvanising unit
-- 100 million marks for joining technology
-- 200 million marks for a new cold-rolling mill
-- 150 million marks for a new electric furnace

Ekkehard Schulz, chairman of Thyssen Stahl AG, steel division of industry group Thyssen AG, in a speech to workers gave a brief outline of preliminary results from the week-long negotiations with Krupp.
Assuring Thyssen steel workers that the brunt of any job cuts would hit Krupp, Schulz said Thyssen's main steel works in Duisburg would emerge as the centre of a new, modern European steel giant.
Here are some excerpts from his speech:
-- Thyssen will have industrial control and a majority of at least 60 percent
-- "Europe's largest producer of flat steel products will emerge with 15 million tonnes of crude steel output a year."
-- Hot metal production will be concentrated at Thyssen's Duisburg steel works and Huettenwerke-Krupp-Mannesmann
-- Talks about coke requirements must be held with Ruhrkohle AG, but in the long-term a new coke oven plant at the works harbor on the Rhine is indispensible
-- Four blast furnaces will be in full operation, full utilisation of the steel works and hot-rolling mills
-- The compact strip rolling mill, which was ordered on March 17, will be built in Bruckhausen as approved by the supervisory board in November
-- Full employment in cold-rolled strip and galvanising units
-- As already approved, the rail finishing shop for 120 metre rails will be built in Bruckhausen
-- In Dortmund (Krupp-Hoesch's main steel works) we want to strengthen cold-rolled strip and galvanising facilities
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150
